offending_extra_words: provided that no settlement imposing any obligation on the Company shall be made without the Company's prior written consent
(provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission on the Company shall be made without the Company's prior written consent)
reasons: All ten atomic elements of the preferred position are present in the inserted clause: defend and indemnify, Customer plus affiliates, the four coverage triggers (IP infringement of Site/Services/materials, breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and notice/control/cooperation mechanics. The Customer-indemnity limitation is conditionally met because no Customer indemnity exists anywhere in the document.

The fallback is a separate bargain and fails on its own terms: no modification, combination or specification exclusions; no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies; and no 3x annual fees super-cap. This does not matter because the locked preferred level is complete.

Minimality fails: 'and hold harmless' extends beyond the preferred prose's defend-and-indemnify duty, and the settlement-consent proviso adds a settlement-control mechanic beyond the preferred 'notice, control, cooperation' triad. Delete 'and hold harmless' and the parenthetical proviso to bring the insertion to strict minimality.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is a new lettered subsection (c) that leaves clause 9(a)-(b) and the Globix carve-out untouched, uses only defined terms (HDI, Company, Site, Services, Content, Marks) and introduces no contradiction or dangling mechanic.
Severity is low because the non-minimal extras (hold-harmless, settlement consent) both operate in the Customer's favour and do not weaken any counterparty-facing protection.
